To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

total-dose failure mechanisms of integrated circuits are dose-rate dependent and that the total-dose failure of integrated circuits in space radiation environments can be significantly different from that observed in laboratory environments.
total-dose hardness varies significantly between dose rates of 100 to 0.01 rad(Si)/sec for both transistors and ICs, and the radiation response of ICs is governed by radiation effects in transistors.

the total-dose failure mechanisms of SRAMS in space radiation environments can be quite different than those at higher laboratory dose rates, and that the total-dote hardness of SRAMS can vary significantly between laboratory and low-dose-rate (0.02 rad/s) environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
total-dose radiation effects in integrated circuits.
understanding the mechanisms that limit total-dose hardness in space environments.
the total-dose radiation response of integrated circuits, particularly SRAMs, in space environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
total dose hardness of integrated circuits is not a simple function of total dose alone.
the dominant total-dose failure mechanisms of ICs in laboratory and space environments are quite different.
the dominant total-dose failure mechanisms of SRAMS vary significantly between laboratory and low dose rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dominant mechanisms for radiation-induced degradation are the same in laboratory and space, but the dose-rate dependence of these mechanisms is quite different.
radiation-induced interface states in SiO2 are not only a function of total dose, but are also a function of dose rate.
the total-dose response of CMOS ICs is a complex, multi-variable function of dose, dose rate, bias conditions, and temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dose rate of a total-dose radiation environment must be specified in order to predict accurately the radiation hardness of ICs.

the radiation hardness of ICs and transistors is strongly dependent on the dose rate and that the dominant failure mechanism in a space radiation environment may be quite different from that observed at higher dose rates.
IC total-dose failure mechanisms in space are not the same as those observed at the much higher dose rates specified in the DoD test guidelines.
